verdict.rationale: DeepSeek has a dedicated Rate Limit & Isolation page. It documents per-model concurrency limits (e.g. 2500/500), SSE keep-alive behavior under load, and 429 semantics on the error-codes page. Higher limits come through a free capacity-expansion request rather than published tiers. The limits are concurrency-based, not requests or tokens per unit time, and the evidence does not show the actual 429 response body. Missing for 10: documented requests/tokens-per-minute limits, a published tier scaling schedule, a concrete 429 response example, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read documented rate limits — requests and tokens per unit time, how tiers scale, and what a 429 looks like — before I hit them in production

citations.quote: A dedicated "Rate Limit & Isolation" page documents concurrency limits (pricing page tables show per-model concurrency, e.g. 2500/500)

If you need higher concurrency, you can submit a capacity expansion request. We will match the appropriate concurrency based on your actual business needs. There is no additional cost for capacity expansion.
